query: Dependency scan fails with incorrect file path when input contains @ in directory name on Windows
reference_answer:
Some context of how we handled this initially at https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/22642#discussion_r3401828982. I don't think the current PRs are solving this right, so I'm writing down some thoughts on the fix. Please don't use agents to get it done quickly.

### Problem

We're currently reserving glob patterns for future use, but we still want to allow escaping so it works if you need to use paths that look like glob patterns. But of course in Windows this can be ambiguous:

- `C:\root\@src\index.html`
- `.\@src\index.html`
- `./path\@src\index.html` (mixed slashes for some reason)

### Possible ideas

A lot of this behaviour is based on tsdown's. From what I can tell, even if you use paths that look like glob, e.g. `./a*(z)/index.ts`, and it uses tinyglobby to glob, it can still match the file as is. Like a file literally named `./a*(z)/index.ts`.

So maybe the fix here is that if the path exists (resolved from root), then we don't need to check for glob patterns? In that case, we also likely don't need to unescape anymore? (Could be breaking if someone relied on it before though)

cc @sapphi-red

Rollup docs does not explain what value `RenderedModule.code` contains. But from the name and the implementation ([code](https://github.com/rollup/rollup/blob/186b352f3b028c5733c47dadacd565e303567e9d/src/Chunk.ts#L1350-L1384)), I think it should return the code after the treeshaking was applied. So I think it is expected to be removed if the variable is not used. In fact, Rollup seems to remove the unused variables and the directives ([tweaked stackblitz with Vite 7](https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-dmwtfi2p?file=vite.config.ts,package.json,node_modules%2F.pnpm%2Frollup%404.60.1%2Fnode_modules%2Frollup%2Fdist%2Frollup.d.ts)).

Rollup also seems to remove the comment if the adjacent code is removed (see the stackblitz example linked above). On the other hand, Rolldown removes comments other than the ones listed [here](https://rolldown.rs/reference/OutputOptions.comments) and Vite disables all of these when minify is enabled (i.e. all comments will be removed). If you turn them on, it will be included in the output, which I guess is not desired. Even if Rolldown aligned the comments behavior with Rollup, it won't work in some cases as the comment will be removed if the adjacent code is removed.

If it works, I think it would be safer to inject a function call instead of a comment (e.g. `astroHeadInject()`) and remove that call in `renderChunk`.

This is slightly different from the normal lockfile (`./pnpm.lock`). Even if Vite exposed the option, I'm not sure if Vite or the monorepo tool can have a proper document about this.

As an alternative, I think we can add
```js
{
  path: '.rush/temp/shrinkwrap-deps.json',
  // Included in lockfile
  checkPatchesDir: false,
  manager: 'pnpm',
},
```

In your case (npm `file:` + `--install-links`), the dependency files changes without the lockfile being changed even though it's not a symlink.
If removing `--install-links` works fine, I'd recommend that. If not, maybe using a package manager that updates the lock file when the content changes could solve your problem (I'm not sure if there're any though).

reference_answer:
More simple reproduction: https://stackblitz.com/edit/github-jxnpwg49?file=server%2Fapp.ts,vite.config.ts,package.json&terminal=build (needs to run locally as prisma does not work in stackblitz)

It seems prisma generates `node_modules/.prisma/client` and imports that from `node_modules/@prisma/client/default.js` by `require('.prisma/client/default')`.
While `require('.prisma/client/default')` works, Vite does not support that because it's not supported for imports (i.e. `import '.prisma/client/default'` errors with `ERR_INVALID_MODULE_SPECIFIER` ([spec](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#resolution-and-loading-algorithm:~:text=If%20packageName%20starts,Module%20Specifier%20error.)). Technically, Vite should allow that to be resolved for `require`, but I think it's better to be avoided and the default generated location should be changed on prisma side.

For a workaround, you can change the location.
https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/setup-and-configuration/generating-prisma-client#the-location-of-prisma-client
For example, update `schema.prisma` to include the following code:
```
generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
  output = "../node_modules/@prisma/client-generated"
}
```
and update the import to use `@prisma/client-generated` (instead of `@prisma/client`).
